subject: Renewal + Upgrade path: pricing stitch and temporary price hold request
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@latticecloud.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@latticecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal + upgrade interest — next steps and ask for usage export

Hi Sofia and team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — great to see LatticeCloud adoption growing across search and chat. Per note, you mentioned interest in renewing your platform contract (annual) and adding the dedicated inference tier for higher throughput on the recommender workload. To put a concrete proposal together I need two quick things from procurement: a 3‑month rolling usage export (tokens / embeddings / peak qps) and the billing SLA boundaries you require for the new tier.

High level we can do the following if you confirm intent before Sep 10: 
- Hold current hosted pricing for 90 days post-signature for the base tier (price-hold window).
- Offer staged uplift credits for the first 3 months of the dedicated tier to offset onboarding — modeled as a $Xk/month credit that declines over time.
- Provide invoice smoothing (monthly amortized over the first 6 months) so the first quarter doesn’t spike cashflow.

I attached a short usage snapshot that helps us size the uplift (LatticeCloud_Monthly_Usage_Snapshot_Aug2026.pdf). If you can send the raw export and confirm whether legal requires any redlines up front, I’ll loop in Marissa and Ben to draft a buy-side-friendly addendum.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call early next week to run the numbers and confirm the canaries for rollout. What times work for you?

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0199
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

Attachment: LatticeCloud_Monthly_Usage_Snapshot_Aug2026.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@latticecloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@latticecloud.com>, LatticeCloud Finance <procure@latticecloud.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + upgrade interest — next steps and ask for usage export

Jonas — thanks, appreciate the clear path. We did a quick internal pull and attached our internal usage export for the past 90 days (summarized). Procurement is particularly focused on: firm pricing for the upgraded tier, any early termination/true-up mechanics, and certainty around invoice timing.

We like the idea of a temporary price hold but need a documented commitment timeline from Redwood so our procurement/legal can sync. Can you confirm: 
- How long the price hold remains valid after a signed LOI?
- Whether the staged uplift credits appear as invoice-level credits or as a one-time rebate?

Also copying finance — can your team accept Net-45 invoices plus a one-time PO for the first tranche? If finance is OK, procurement can expedite.

Best,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Product Ops | LatticeCloud
sofia.ramos@latticecloud.com

Attachment: LatticeCloud_Usage_Export_JunJulAug2026.csv (csv, 12KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@latticecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + upgrade interest — draft terms and conditional plan

Sofia — thanks for the export, that was super helpful. Quick answers first: 
- Price hold: we can commit to a 30‑day binding LOI window (signed LOI → 30 days of guaranteed list pricing for the base tier), extendable to 60 days with a small administrative deposit (refundable credit on first invoice).
- Credits: staged uplift credits will be applied as invoice-level credits in the first three monthly invoices; we can optionally convert to a one-time rebate in month 2 if that simplifies your finance reconciliation.
- Net-45: Redwood can accept Net-45 on the initial PO for the base tier; dedicated capacity upfront is typically billed at activation (we can amortize across Q1 to smooth).

Below is the operational proposal we’d like to surface to legal and procurement — if this is acceptable I’ll ask Marissa to produce a draft addendum for review: 
1) Term: 12 months base renewal for hosted tier + 12 month minimum for dedicated capacity activation (kicked by first activation date).
2) Price-hold mechanics: Signed LOI by Sep 10 → 30 day guaranteed price hold on base tier; administrative deposit option to extend to 60 days (applied as credit to first invoice).
3) Staged uplift credits: $30k credit month 1, $20k month 2, $10k month 3 — applied as invoice credits.
4) Invoice smoothing: dedicated activation billed 50% at activation, remainder amortized across next 5 invoices.
5) True-up: quarterly true-up against actual token/embedding usage; overages billed at committed rate for 60 days then at list thereafter unless a revision is agreed.
6) Ops: we’ll designate a technical onboarding lead and reserve burst capacity during the first 14 days of go‑live (no extra charge for the buffer).

Attaching a one-page draft addendum to accelerate legal redlines (Draft_Addendum_Renewal_Upgrade_2026.docx). Can Marissa/Ben/Olga confirm legal and finance are fine with these levers and whether we need to convert credits to rebates for LatticeCloud’s AP process?

If Sofia is good with this approach, propose a 30–45 minute redline call on Thu (9/3) at 10am PT.

—
Jonas

Attachment: Draft_Addendum_Renewal_Upgrade_2026.docx (docx, 72KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + upgrade interest — draft terms and conditional plan

Looping in legal/finance as requested. Quick notes: 
- Legal (Olga): I reviewed the draft addendum at a high level — the price-hold and staged credits are fine, we should add a simple cap on cumulative credits to avoid open-ended exposure. I’ll propose language this afternoon.
- Finance (Ben): Net-45 is acceptable; for the deposit-to-extend flow we need the deposit routed as a refundable credit line item in NetSuite (Ben, can we map this to a specific AR code?).

Jonas — feel free to go ahead and book the 9/3 redline slot; I’ll be on the call with Orca Legal. Olga, Ben — appreciate quick turnaround.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0144
